newsitem.title: UK: British futures body welcomes derivatives plan.
newsitem.headline: British futures body welcomes derivatives plan.

text.p: Britain's Futures and Options Association (FOA) said on Monday it welcomed a recent government announcement on the use of derivatives by unit trusts and investment funds that would avoid the need for new legislation.
"The FOA strongly supports the view that effective self-regulation in this area is preferable to introducing new tax legislation," it said in a statement.

Such legislation, it said, could restrict development of innovative unit trusts. Unit trusts, similar to mutual funds in the United States, pool together people's money for investing in various securities.

The FOA said that following discussions with the Association of Unit Trusts and Investment Funds (AUTIF) and the FOA, the government had agreed to the industry's approach to deal with the emerging use of derivatives by unit trusts through making amendments to a revised Statement of Recommended Practice.

The FOA said it has been in talks with the Securities and Investments Board, the top British financial watchdog, over ways to introduce unit trust inncations such as performance-related fees or guaranteed funds.
"The prospect of uncertain or inflexible tax treatment would have undermined the commrcial value of these changes," the FOA statement said.
